pr.title: fix(restack): reconcile remote-only commits before force-pushing
pr.body: fix(restack): reconcile remote-only commits before force-pushing When a stack branch's remote tip has commits the local branch lacks (e.g. a commit made directly on GitHub), `sync`/`restack` now refresh the branches' tracking refs and offer to cherry-pick those commits in before force-pushing. Previously the push was rejected and git-stk looped on "the remote has moved on — run sync" with no way to reconcile. Closes #270 - 🟣 ~~[fix(submit): refresh a stale overview row that has since merged (#273)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/273)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[fix(restack): reconcile remote-only commits before force-pushing (#272)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/272)~~ (merged) 👈 - `main` --- Stack managed by [git-stk](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk)

expected.description: Remote-only commits are found by patch id alone, so after a parent is squash-merged and the branch rebased, the remote's old commits look missing locally and restack offers to cherry-pick work already present.
